lore_example: The Candor's hierarchy runs from the Luminary and Praelucent through the Chapter and Canons of the Rose to parish wick-priests and junior Tapers.
The Lanthorn is a major employer whose ordinary work includes keys, cleaning, pilgrim fees, crowd control and practical assistance; Verger Dunstan Pike keeps the nave keys.
Sexton Noll Fitch digs and tends graves, rings the name-knell and chalks each newly buried name on Saint Maren's charnel-door lintel.
Ringers sound offices, feasts, alarms and funerals; Perrinstide is their feast, when the bells are washed and greased.
Grey-coated clerks copy and file records, issue licences and badges, carry packets, observe crowds and investigate claims concerning the Emblem.
Dame Aldith lives enclosed in the Ilvane anchorhold, receives alms and trades verses for honest news through the squint.
The masons' lodge is one of Ombreval's strongest trade powers and carries its grievance against the glaziers from the sealed trial of F.288.
Cinder Row's glaziers make, paint, lead and repair cathedral glass; the Sparr line remains tied to the Great Rose and to the guild's feud with the masons.
Timber, scaffolding, roofs, jetties and overhead bridges are constant parts of Ombreval's building life, although no separate carpenters' guild is established.
The smith is one of the twelve trades depicted in the Great Rose, shown at a black-red fire with yellow sparks.
Great Ambrelle and the lesser bells were cast at Coswald's Yard; Saint Perrin began as a founder's boy and learned to tune bronze by palm and jawbone.
The Wickmarket trades in wax, tallow, wicks and lamps; Osanne Vell supplies the Lanthorn's candles.
Lamplighters serve under the Wickmarket chandlers, whistle the three-note wick-call and leave one public lantern dark each night as Belwyn's lamp.
The Unwalled include a rope-walker, and Petronel Roper is supplied as an approved trade byname.
The painter of the Rose panel showing the Luminary had never visited Ostrelle and imagined its cathedral as a smaller Lanthorn.
Ferrant owns unusually fine lenses and measuring instruments; Emeric Sault pointedly asks who grinds those lenses and pays for them.
Ombreval turns Brede wool into finished cloth through weaving, fulling, tenting and dyeing; Tam Rud is a journeyman fuller on the Cut.
The drapers paid to roof the Draper's Reach, where cloth is measured against the standard ell of Ombreval.
The old tanneries burned in F.157, while Tanners' Slip and Skinners' Court preserve the city's leather trades in their names.
Mabbe, remembered among the Unwalled's old pass-names, was a washerwoman of the Cut.
Dob was a rag-picker and Pin a rope-picker; both survive in the Unwalled's recent funeral and pass-name history.
Boat-families pole freight between Brede, Ombreval, Harne and Salorge; Wyn Alder is a working boatwoman beyond the south wall.
Maren's Green is the fish and eel market under eel smoke; Wyn Alder combines boat work with eel trading.
Serle cargo is unloaded beyond the south wall and moved through the river gate by cart and porter to warehouses, markets and cloth halls.
Freight brokers are part of the river economy based at Maren's Green, matching cargo with boats, carriers and storage.
Grigor Ashe's lawful living is the salt road: Salorge salt is brought upriver, weighed at Lowmarket and stored near the Tallage.
Pan-workers and salt-rakers work at Salorge, while salt-hands accompany or unload the upriver trade.
Wyn Alder walks pilgrims to old Cut landmarks for a penny, while vergers guide paying visitors inside the Lanthorn.
Merchants know Ombreval as a toll town with honest weights, fair tolls and crowds that turn the window into custom.
Annet, an old pass-name, sold cress by the Gradine; the squares also support honey, food, fish and licensed pilgrim-badge sellers.
Lise Copp keeps a pawnshop facing the Tally Bridge, valuing pledges while money and illicit pages move across the same counter.
Corin Copp writes bills of lading by day; Fabric, Church, court and merchant records create extensive copying, accounting and book work.
Tallage officials weigh grain, cloth, salt and river cargo against chained standards and record the tolls under formal oath.
The baker is depicted among the Great Rose's trades, while bread prices, famine and Wet Alms make bread a public concern.
Butchers feasted on the ox roasted on the frozen Cut in F.229, and slaughter-month is depicted in the Great Rose.
Brewing is one of the Great Rose's month-labours; Malt Passage is an approved name for a passage beneath a malt-house.
The core explicitly names cooks as citizens with lives beyond the cathedral plot, and the Lanthorn and taverns maintain kitchens.
Renna Tapster keeps the Bell and Ladle from the crier's first call until the last argument goes home.
The core reserves nearby farms and mills as necessary parts of Ombreval's food supply, though no individual mill is fixed yet.
Doctor Aubin Ferrant makes sick-calls, Mother Gude gathers and sells simples, and midwives carry parish-specific knowledge around birth and the Passing.
Magister Emeric Sault reads the mathematical arts at Ostrelle, while Aubin Ferrant measures the light and corresponds with distant scholars.
Ede runs messages for a bell-coin, while Crier Jos Brant carries official words around the five squares and posts them at the Bellstand.
Watchmen appear in city rumor and the Old Sluice has a keeper; the exact secular watch hierarchy remains open canon.
The Glaziers' Trial is recorded by a Chapter notary and argued by a lodge proctor before the Praelucent and provosts.

lore_locations: Gallows or execution site not yet fixed
lore_example: Saint Gaudry asked the hangman whether the knot was well tied before he was executed for burning the false customs ledger.
The Great Rose depicts ploughing, sowing, pruning, shearing, haymaking, reaping and threshing, while wool comes from the sheep-hills of the Combs.
Ombreval depends on physical and seasonal labour, from Colm Attergate's work on the west towers to hired hands moving materials, cleaning yards and filling gaps between specialised trades.
